page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. In the left margin, a bracket marks the list of vices at "erit nothus". Below the text, the catchword "Ex" stands at the right.

main_text.p: mentis nomen accepit: quum moribus eius (nouit enim vulpes ad tempus dissimulare) tunc aptius id esse videretur. Hic, quum Galli contra Caesarem faceret, Roma à Caesarianis vi occupata, ad S. Angeli castrum confugit: illis tamen, quum arctius premeretur, coactum se dedidit. Carolus vero nimis obseruans Pontificis, priscis eum luxurijs mox restituit. Quae vero militum, in ea urbis occupatione, virtutes fuerint, quomodo Cardinales tractauerint, & thesauros expilauerint, longa narratione vix comprehendi posset. Quare in aliud tempus ea Funccius ille referuat. Ex Henrico Pantaleone: Clemens pontifex, cum rege Gallorum contra Imperatorem conspirans, à ducibus Caroli, cum Cardinalibus & urbe capitur: ac ciuibus occisis, miru in modum à Germanis militibus ludificatur, anno Domini 1527. Ex Ioannis Tilij Chronico: Redimi-tur postea Clemens captiuus, 4oooo[?] florenis. De isto Clemente, in quodam commentario super articulis magistrorum Parisiensium legitur, quod fuerit nothus, veneficus, homicida, leno, Simoniacus, Sodomita, periurus, stuprator, raptor, geomanticus, sacrilegus, & omnium scelerum artifex. De quo poeta quidam cecinit:

p.i: Clementi nomen dedit inclementia fati, Bellorum hic fomes, sanctorum lerna malorum.

page.notes: The bracket at the left margin beside "erit nothus" is a typographical mark, not a note. The numeral "4oooo" is hard to read and is marked [?]. The text in the left margin is not printed text, so the verse lines are the only margin-adjacent text, and they are in the main text. The line "Bellorum hic fomes, canctorum lerna malorum" is printed "canctorum"; it is transcribed here as "sanctorum" by reading and should be checked against the scan.
